channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Former State Security Service officials sentenced to lengthy prison terms
item.description: Uzbekistan's Military Court sentenced former officials of the State Security Service (SSS) on November 27. Former deputy head General Gayratilla Yoziyev received 15 years, and former head of SSS Internal Security Colonel Alijon Ashurov received 17 years. Other officials were also sentenced to 15 to 17 years. Yoziyev was found guilty of extortion, illegal detention, and abuse of power.

item.title: Uzbekistan Launches International Year of Sustainable and Resilient Tourism
item.description: Uzbekistan has announced the launch of the International Year of Sustainable and Resilient Tourism (2027) in Tashkent. This initiative, developed by Uzbekistan and supported by over 80 countries, was adopted by the UN General Assembly in 2024. The event was attended by UN Tourism Secretary-General and representatives from more than 45 nations.

item.title: Moscow to Increase Migrant Work Permit Fees from January 1, 2027
item.description: Moscow authorities will raise the cost of work permits for migrants starting January 1, 2027. The Moscow City Duma approved amendments to tax legislation, increasing the monthly fee. This decision is attributed to rising average salaries in sectors popular among foreigners. Similar increases are expected in other regions.

item.title: Three Former Top Managers of Kazakhstan Railways Arrested for Corruption
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee has detained three former top managers of 'KTZ-Cargo Transportation' on suspicion of corruption. Vladimir Petrov, Kairat Kabylov, and Azamat Sembay were arrested for two months by court order. The committee is conducting an investigation to determine all circumstances of the case.

item.title: Cameras Found in School Toilet in Atyrau, Kazakhstan; Data Breaches Also Reported
item.description: Prosecutors in Atyrau, Kazakhstan, discovered cameras in a school toilet, compromising the privacy of over 1,400 students. The regional prosecutor's office also reported other violations, including personal data breaches affecting over 4,000 children across the region. Violators have been held accountable and rights restored.

item.title: Rustam Emomali's Increased Public Appearances Alongside Father Fuels Succession Speculation
item.description: Rustam Emomali, the eldest son of Tajikistan's president, is appearing more frequently with his father at official events and on state television. This increased visibility, including jointly welcoming Russian President Putin, has intensified discussions about potential power transition ahead of next year's presidential election.

item.title: Astana Intensifies Snow Removal Efforts Amidst Heavy Snowfall
item.description: Astana's communal services are operating in an intensified mode due to continuous snowfall. Snow removal operations are ongoing around the clock. On November 27, heavy vehicles removed over 1,200 cubic meters of snow. Over 600 special vehicles and 500 road workers were mobilized overnight.

item.title: Jizzakh Water Official Arrested for Promising to Erase Debt
item.description: An employee of "Jizzakh Suv Ta'minoti" JSC has been apprehended for allegedly demanding 9 million soums. The official reportedly promised to erase a 100 million soum water debt for an entrepreneur and install a new water meter in exchange for the bribe.

item.title: Kazatomprom Clarifies Official Status of Second Arrested Employee
item.description: Kazatomprom has clarified the official status of an employee arrested by the National Security Committee. The company stated that the arrested individual is a chief manager of a department, not a top executive. The National Security Committee reported the arrest of Kuanych Omurbekov and chief manager Baikulov, suspecting them of involvement in a corruption scheme.

item.title: WADA President Comments on Kazakh Athlete Yasmina Toksanbayeva's Disqualification
item.description: WADA President Witold Bańka commented on the case of Kazakh athlete Yasmina Toksanbayeva, disqualified from the 2026 Asian Games marathon race. He expressed sympathy but stated the issue is not doping-related and falls under the international federation's jurisdiction. Toksanbayeva lost her gold medal due to non-compliant shoe sole thickness.

item.title: Kazatomprom Clarifies Status of Second Suspect in Criminal Case
item.description: Kazatomprom has clarified the position of E. Baikulova, the second individual mentioned in a criminal case by the National Security Committee. The company stated Baikulova is a chief manager in a department, not a top executive. The clarification comes after media reports suggested another top manager was arrested. Both Baikulova and a former chief production director were arrested for two months.

item.title: Kazakhstan Conducts Security Checks on Polling Stations Ahead of Maslikhat Elections
item.description: Over 10,000 polling stations across Kazakhstan are undergoing security checks in preparation for the maslikhat elections scheduled for November 29. The Ministry of Internal Affairs confirmed that anti-terrorism protection requirements are being verified. Police will maintain public order on election day.

item.title: Harvard Analysts Develop Four Scenarios for Russia's Future by 2030
item.description: Harvard analysts have developed four scenarios outlining potential political and economic changes in Russia by 2030. The study examines the possible outcomes of the war in Ukraine, Russia's international standing, and the future of Putin's leadership, assessing which scenario is most likely to occur.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Changes to Judge Disciplinary Commission Structure
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering amendments to the Law "On Bodies of Judicial Self-Governance" to reform the disciplinary commission of the Judicial Council. The proposed changes aim to include lawyers, legal scholars, and human rights defenders alongside judges, enhancing accountability and transparency in disciplinary proceedings against judges.

item.title: Uzbekistan Unveils New Transport Strategy Focused on Roads and Investment
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev reviewed Uzbekistan's new transport strategy, emphasizing quality roads, significant investments, and international integration. He visited a road construction research center and met with investors, highlighting the importance of scientific research and modern technologies in the transport sector.

item.title: Kazakhstan Discusses Role of Maslikhats Under New Constitution
item.description: Experts in Almaty discussed the role, powers, and development prospects of maslikhats (local representative bodies) under Kazakhstan's new constitution. Key issues raised included increasing the autonomy of local representative bodies, strengthening deputy accountability, and enhancing public engagement.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Coal Enterprises Request Government Permission for Summer Exports
item.description: Coal mining enterprises in Kyrgyzstan's Sulyukta are seeking government permission to export coal during the summer months. Currently, export is restricted, and companies prioritize supplying the domestic market in autumn and winter. Summer exports would help prevent coal degradation from prolonged storage and address falling domestic demand.

item.title: Kazakhstan Opens Registration for Citizenship Test Applicants
item.description: Kazakhstan begins accepting applications for the citizenship test on November 27. The National Testing Center will receive applications until December 7, with the test scheduled for December 8. Applicants can register via the National Testing Center's website or app. The test covers Kazakh language, Constitution basics, and history.

item.title: Taliban Security Commission Meets Under Leader Akhundzada
item.description: The Taliban's security commission convened a meeting led by the group's leader, Hibatullah Akhundzada. The meeting was held at the Taliban-run Arg, according to a statement from the office.

item.title: Kazakhstan Court Sentences Activist Sanjar Bokayev; Over 13,000 Foreign Fighters Die in Ukraine
item.description: A court in Almaty has issued a verdict in the case of activist Sanjar Bokayev. Over 13,000 individuals from Central Asian countries fighting for Russia in Ukraine have died, including Kazakh citizens. The prosecutor's office issued a warning ahead of the maslikhat elections.

item.title: UN Warns Child Marriage Violates Rights and Harms Health and Education in Afghanistan
item.description: The United Nations has declared child marriage a human rights violation, warning of its severe consequences on children's physical and mental health and education. This statement comes as child marriage is permitted under Afghanistan's Taliban-endorsed Regulation on Marital Separation.

item.title: Uzbekistan's economic growth to exceed global average by 2026, IMF projects
item.description: The International Monetary Fund has released its 2026 economic growth projections for 191 countries. Uzbekistan is expected to achieve an average growth rate more than double the global average. The IMF's new economic forecasts provide a detailed outlook for various nations.

item.title: Medal of Fallen Uzbek Soldier to Return Home from Poland
item.description: A "For Courage" medal belonging to Urun Basar Kuzdaev, an Uzbek soldier who died in World War II, will be returned to Uzbekistan. The medal was discovered in Poland during exhumation work and handed over to Uzbek diplomats. Cooperation in preserving historical monuments was also discussed.

item.title: First apartments in 'Intymak' mortgage complex to be delivered soon
item.description: The head of the Presidential Administration, Kanybek Tumanbaev, inspected the 'Intymak' housing complex under construction by the State Mortgage Company. He emphasized that the premium-class apartments, priced at $1,400 per square meter through state mortgage, are superior to economy-class housing. The complex will feature ample parking, a school, kindergarten, and recreational areas.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Argentina Sign Memorandum on Aviation Cooperation
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and Argentina have signed a memorandum of understanding and cooperation in the field of civil aviation. The agreement aims to establish sustainable professional ties between the aviation authorities of both countries. It will facilitate the exchange of professional experience, technical knowledge, and information, expanding Kyrgyzstan's international aviation partnerships.

item.title: Pavlodar Region: Lands Valued at 115 Million Tenge Returned to State
item.description: The Prosecutor's Office of Pavlodar region has successfully recovered state-owned lands, strategically important for the development of Ekibastuz's coal industry, valued at 115 million tenge. The lands were leased to "Arman kala Limited" but were used for purposes other than intended, hindering industrial infrastructure development. The court ruled to forcibly seize the lands.

item.title: Uzbekistan Extends Customs Benefits for Light Industry Until 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan has extended customs duty exemptions on imported raw materials and components for the textile industry until early 2030. Export revenue return periods for textile companies will be extended to 365 days until January 1, 2028, with no penalties for delays. The government will also support cost reduction initiatives and subsidize artificial fiber imports.

item.title: CIA Waterboarded More Detainees Post-9/11 Than Previously Known, Documents Suggest
item.description: Newly released documents indicate the CIA waterboarded more detainees after 9/11 than previously acknowledged, possibly using a site north of Kabul, Afghanistan. While the agency admitted to waterboarding three individuals, a former translator's account suggests the practice was more common and occurred at a black site known as Salt Pit.

item.title: Uzbekistan Consumer Rights Federation Reports on Five Years of Activity
item.description: The Federation of Consumer Rights Protection Societies of Uzbekistan held a conference summarizing its 2021-2025 activities. The federation received 65,649 appeals, resolving 93.9% of them, and recovered 279.4 billion UZS in material and moral damages. Most appeals concerned trade, gas, electricity, and communal services.

item.title: Bishkek City Hall Reminds Residents of Coal Bases and Solid Fuel Prices for Winter
item.description: Bishkek City Hall has announced that coal bases are operating in the capital's districts, offering solid fuel for the upcoming winter. Prices for "Kara-Keche" coal range from 7,000 soms per ton, while "Shabyrkyul" costs 7,800 soms per ton. Various districts have different quantities of coal available.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Assures Sufficient Fuel Reserves to Meet Year-End Demand
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has sufficient reserves of gasoline and diesel fuel to meet demand until the end of the year, according to a government meeting. Officials noted that current stocks, including those in transit, are adequate. The government plans to continue subsidies and review support mechanisms for the fuel sector, addressing modernization of refineries and trade.

item.title: Uzbekistan Grants Customs Authorities Investigation Powers for Pyrotechnics Cases
item.description: Uzbekistan's Senate has approved a law granting customs authorities enhanced investigation powers for certain pyrotechnics-related offenses. This amendment to the Criminal Procedure Code aims to improve the fight against customs violations, particularly concerning undeclared goods. The law also modifies the Criminal Code regarding evasion of customs duties.

item.title: Four Civil Servants Fired in Zhambyl Region for Gambling
item.description: Four civil servants in the Zhambyl region have been dismissed for participating in gambling. One specialist transferred over 23 million tenge to a gaming account. This action violates a September 2024 law prohibiting civil servants from engaging in gambling, which is grounds for dismissal. The measures aim to prevent addiction, reduce corruption, and enhance public trust.

item.title: Two Kazatomprom Top Managers Detained for Two Months
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee announced the detention of two top managers from the national atomic company Kazatomprom. A pre-trial detention of two months was imposed on the former production director and a department manager. The detentions are related to an ongoing investigation involving former leadership of Samruk-Kazyna and Kazakhstan Temir Zholy.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Introduce Criminal Liability for Developers Housing Unfinished Buildings
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to introduce criminal liability for developers who allow people to move into apartment buildings before they are officially commissioned. The Senate reviewed a law that will amend the Urban Planning Code, obligating clients and contractors to prevent such occupancy. This measure aims to ensure resident safety and protect property rights.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Fine Owners of Unregistered Domestic Animals Starting 2028
item.description: Uzbekistan will begin penalizing owners of unregistered domestic animals, including cats and dogs, from January 1, 2028. Owners must register their pets in a unified electronic database before this date. This measure aims to combat livestock theft, track diseases, and control the spread of stray animals.

item.title: EU Prepares New Defense Funding Program Amid US Uncertainty
item.description: The European Union is developing a new defense financing program worth tens of billions of euros to reduce reliance on US military capabilities. The initiative, expected in the second half of 2027, will include loans and grants. Priorities are integrated air and missile defense, intelligence, and surveillance.

item.title: Uzbekistan Establishes Criminal Liability for Occupying Unfinished Homes
item.description: Uzbekistan's Senate has approved a law establishing criminal liability for individuals and officials who facilitate the occupation of unfinished apartment buildings. The law also amends the Urban Development Code, obligating developers to prevent such illegal settlements. This aims to protect citizens' housing rights and property.

item.title: Kazakhstan Honors Laborers in Ulytau Region's Agricultural Year-End Ceremony
item.description: In the heart of Kazakhstan, the Ulytau region celebrated its agricultural workers. The event in Zhezkazgan recognized leading farmers and specialists for their contributions to food security. Regional officials presented awards and emphasized the importance of agricultural development for employment and well-being.

item.title: Kazatomprom Reports Nine-Month Financial Results, Revenue Up 16%
item.description: Kazatomprom has released its nine-month financial report, showing consolidated revenue nearing 1.4 trillion tenge, a 16% increase year-on-year. Operational profit exceeded 560 billion tenge, with net profit around 479 billion tenge. Uranium production and sales volumes also rose by 10%.
